definition: Social refers to how a person functions in relation to other people and social situations. In this packet, changes in social functioning means gradual differences in how someone manages interactions or participation with others.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define the term “social” as “how a person functions in relation to other people and social situations.” It only mentions “social functioning” in the context of schizophrenia-related changes.

The claim that “changes in social functioning means gradual differences in how someone manages interactions or participation with others” is not stated in the packet; the packet only says “gradual changes in … social functioning often appear” and does not define social functioning in those terms.

The packet only supports the phrase “gradual changes in social functioning” appearing before first episode of psychosis; it does not define the general term “social” as how a person functions in relation to other people and social situations.
“Manages interactions or participation with others” is an added interpretation that is not stated in the source packet.
